newsitem.title: USA: Corporate hi-grade debt deals stir, Raytheon preps.
newsitem.headline: Corporate hi-grade debt deals stir, Raytheon preps.

text.p: Activity in the investment grade corporate arena is stirring as a $2.5 billion Raytheon Co debt offering is prepped to come to market and several others are on tap, dealers said.
"Tuesday's business should include Chrysler's deal as well as a utility offering," said one syndicate source. "More paper is on the horizon as Raytheon's deal is rumored for next week."
Slated for Tuesday's business is OGE Energy Corp unit Oklahoma Gas & Electric Co's $250 million in Aa3/AA-minus rated offering.

The deal is expected to include $125 million in 20-year debt, putable in the seventh year, and is expected to be underwritten by Lehman Brothers, players said. Price talk on the issue is seen at 26 to 28 basis points over Treasuries.

The second tranche is expected to consist of a $125 million 30-year debt issue, putable in the tenth year, and is expected to be underwritten by Merrill Lynch & Co. Price talk on the issue is seen between 38 to 40 basis points over Treasuries.
Also on Tuesday, Chrsyler Corp is expected to sell $500 million in 100-year debentures via Salomon Brothers.
Price talk on Chrysler's 100-year issue was rumored between 80 to 81 basis points over Treasuries, sources said.

Meanwhile, Raytheon Co is expected to sell $2.5 billion in a three-tranche debt offering via Morgan Stanley & Co next week. The deal is expected to include five-year, 10-year and 30-year maturities, dealers said.

Other underwriters on the deal include: Bear Stearns Cos Inc, Credit Suisse First Boston, Merrill Lynch & Co, JP Morgan Securities Inc, Goldman Sachs & Co, Salomon Brothers and Chase Securities, dealers said.
Raytheon recently completed the purchase of Texas Instruments Inc's defense and electronics unit for $2.95 billion.
The unit is a premier supplier of advanced defense systems, including precision-guided weapons, airborne radar and night vision systems.

Raytheon, headquartered in Lexington, Massachusetts, is an international high-technology company which operates in seveal businesses: commercial and defense electronics, engineering and construction, aircraft and major appliances.
Among global issues, Argentina is expected to issue a $750 million seven-year global debt offering via Credit Suisse First Boston, sources said.
Elsewhere, $3.5 billion in 144A private placement junk bond offerings are on tap to come to market, syndicate sources said.
Discovery Zone Inc, the indoor play center company, will look to the junk bond market to finance its emergence from bankruptcy protection, which it filed for in March, 1996, sources said.

Discovery Zone is expected to issue $80 million in five-year 144a senior secured notes via Jefferies & Co. The notes will be sold as units which will also include warrants to purchase up 12.50 percent to 15 percent of the company.
Price talk on Discovery Zone's upcoming issue is seen between 13.25 - 13.50 percent, sources said.
Nextel Communications Inc is also planning a $350 million sale of an exchange pik preferred 12-year issue later in the week, sources said.
Looking ahead, another $500 million in 144a debt is expected to come from supermarket concern, Flemings Cos.
